name: Imagination Effect
fact: Imagining a procedure or concept can be a more effective instructional technique than conventional studying, provided the presentation format is integrated rather than split-attention.
boundary: Applies to learning procedures or concepts; effectiveness depends on the mode of presentation (integrated vs. split-attention).

provenance.title: Cognitive load and the imagination effect
provenance.quote_or_locus: Results on a subsequent test indicated that the Grade 4 students found imagining beneficial to their learning, compared with studying the material but the effect was only obtained using an integrated rather than a split‐attention format
